Feeling lightheaded and nervous before speaking in front of a group is incredibly common. When anxiety kicks in, our bodies often react with shallow breathing, which can easily cause that dizzy sensation. One of the most effective ways to manage this in the moment is to focus on your breathing. Try taking slow, deep breaths from your belly rather than your chest. Inhaling deeply for a count of four and exhaling slowly can help regulate your oxygen levels and signal to your nervous system to calm down.

Along with deep breathing, grounding techniques can help keep you centered. Try pressing your feet firmly into the floor or holding onto a podium to give yourself a physical anchor. It can also help to practice your speech in front of a small, trusted friend group to build your confidence gradually. Remember to be patient with yourself; managing public speaking anxiety takes time, and it is completely okay to take a brief pause during your presentation to catch your breath.
